extra_quotes: We used the AdamW optimizer for 500 000 training iterations, which took approximately one day on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU for the model sizes used here.
Unless stated otherwise, posterior samples from trained FMPE models were generated by integrating the learned ODE with the adaptive Dormand–Prince solver implemented in torchdiffeq.
The learning rate followed a cosine annealing schedule from 1 .0 × 10−3, after a 500-step warm-up, to 1 .0 × 10−6.
Interfacial roughnesses are not included in this proof-of-concept model because of the limitations of the transfer-matrix treatment discussed in the Methods section.

This result should be viewed as a proof of concept for spin-resolved posterior inference rather than as a complete treatment of experimental full-PNR analysis with roughness and additional instrumental effects.
In addition, flow matching inference requires numerical integration of an ODE, which can make raw sampling slower than direct sampling from many discrete normalizing-flow models.
